The error message indicates a storage array capacity issue, not a Kubernetes configuration problem. The specific error is from the Corvane storage array (csi.corvane.io driver), not a Kubernetes issue. This is a storage backend problem that needs to be resolved by cleaning up LUN mappings on the storage array side.

Let me update the ticket with my findings:

input.note:
Root Cause: clickhouse-2 pod is stuck in ContainerCreating due to a storage array capacity issue, not a Kubernetes problem.

Evidence: The pod logs show "MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume pvc-8d21f6c3-2a9e-4b07-9f4d-3e6a1c5b8d90: rpc error: code = Internal desc = csi.corvane.io: CVN-4127: host initiator iqn.1994-05.com.redhat:ip-10-0-93-12 rejected by array cv-array-02: host group hg-k8s-prod reached max LUN mappings (512); retry after mapping cleanup". The persistent volume claim (data-clickhouse-2) is Bound and the node assignment is correct, but the storage array at cv-array-02 has reached its maximum LUN mapping limit (512) for the host group.

Fix: Contact your storage team to perform "mapping cleanup" on the Corvane storage array cv-array-02 for host group hg-k8s-prod. This will free up LUN mappings on the array so the third replica can successfully mount its volume. Once the array cleanup is complete, Kubernetes will automatically retry the volume mount and the pod should transition to Running.
